# Murmuration v2 Test Plan, Risk Mitigations & Verification Criteria

**Date**: 2026-10-19
**Source Analysis**: `_architect/analysis/2026-10-19-murmur-v2-evolution-and-web-foundry.md`

## 1. Test Plan & Quality Assurance

Quality assurance across Phase One requires a multi-layered verification strategy that validates new functionality while rigorously protecting the existing test baseline. Because Murmur already boasts one hundred and forty-three passing unit and integration tests executing in approximately one point three seconds, every new component must integrate cleanly without slowing down the test runner or introducing flaky asynchronous behavior.

The Unit Testing Matrix focuses on the isolated verification of new core logic. For the provider subsystem, tests in `tests/providers.test.ts` will exercise the client interface using injected mock HTTP handlers. These tests will verify correct Authorization header construction, payload formatting for OpenRouter and MeshAPI endpoints, automatic tier classification (validating that code-scanning prompts route to fast models while architecture synthesis prompts route to reasoning models), and resilient error handling during network timeouts or HTTP error codes. For the experience cascading engine, tests in `tests/experience.test.ts` will validate hierarchical inheritance under four distinct permutations: when all three tiers exist, when only repository experience exists, when only user-global experience exists, and when no prior experience exists. The assertions will confirm that project-specific rules consistently take precedence over user rules, that conflicting directives are resolved deterministically, and that new lessons learned during execution are appended to the correct tier without corrupting markdown formatting.

The Integration Testing Matrix validates end-to-end command execution. Tests in `tests/initSemantic.test.ts` will simulate `murmr init --semantic` inside isolated temporary directories. Using mocked provider responses, the tests will verify that repository directory trees and package manifests are ingested, that synthesis requests are generated, and that the resulting `murmur/skills/` and `murmur/instructions/` directories are populated with valid YAML frontmatter that subsequently passes `murmr doctor` validation with zero warnings. In addition, tests in `tests/harness2Experience.test.ts` will verify that `murmr evolve` automatically pulls from the three-tier experience resolver during the Propose phase and writes verified candidate improvements back into `murmur/EXPERIENCE.md` upon successful compilation.

The Regression and Static Verification Pipeline guarantees codebase health. Before any commit is approved, two automated checks must execute synchronously: full TypeScript type-checking (`bun run typecheck`) to ensure strict interface compliance across all new modules, and the complete test suite execution (`bun test`) to ensure all one hundred and forty-three legacy tests continue to pass alongside the new test suites.

The Web Asset and Visual Quality Assurance Protocol validates the public showcase in `website/`. Because the web application is built with vanilla modern technologies, testing involves automated structure checks to ensure that `index.html`, `style.css`, and `app.js` contain valid markup, valid CSS custom properties, and error-free JavaScript execution. The interactive Intermediate Representation playground must be tested to ensure that selecting different target runtimes (such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or Antigravity) instantly updates the preview panel without DOM errors, and that the layout adapts flawlessly across mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports.

## 2. Risks, Mitigations & Failure Modes

Any substantial expansion of an agentic architecture introduces specific technical risks that must be analyzed and mitigated prior to implementation.

The first critical risk is Upstream Provider Rate Limiting and Token Inflation. When developers invoke `murmr init --semantic` on extensive codebases containing hundreds of files, attempting to feed entire repository trees into a single large context window will trigger HTTP four-hundred-twenty-nine rate limit exceptions, slow down execution, and generate excessive API costs. To mitigate this risk, the provider client implements intelligent repository preprocessing. The scanner extracts only structural metadata—such as directory topographies, package manifests, and export signatures—while ignoring bulky dependency directories (`node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`). Furthermore, the auto-routing tier dispatches lightweight summarization tasks to low-cost, high-throughput models before submitting condensed architectural summaries to high-parameter reasoning models. If an upstream gateway returns rate limit or quota errors, the client automatically backs off with exponential jitter and falls back to deterministic rule-based scaffolding without crashing the initialization workflow.

The second critical risk is Experience Contamination and Hallucinatory Memory Drift. Storing contextual memories across three hierarchical tiers introduces the possibility that idiosyncratic conventions from one client project might bleed into unrelated repositories via the global user experience file, or that an LLM agent might append hallucinated or incorrect guidelines into `murmur/EXPERIENCE.md`. To mitigate this failure mode, Murmur enforces strict scoping rules. Project experience is kept strictly sandboxed within the repository's git boundary and is never written upward into the user's global directory without explicit user intervention. Global user experience is restricted to domain-agnostic workflow preferences. Furthermore, before any candidate experience is committed to disk by the Harness squared engine, it must pass deterministic probe validation proving that the recommendation successfully compiles and passes linting checks.

The third critical risk is Scope Creep and Concurrency Thrashing from the Two-Thousand-Agent Swarm Fallacy. In distributed agent systems, there is an enticing temptation to market massive concurrency numbers by spawning unbudgeted agent fleets. In practice, running hundreds of concurrent LLM sessions against commercial API endpoints causes severe connection exhaustion, socket timeouts, and financial ruin. Murmur mitigates this by enforcing strict worker pool limits. Regardless of conceptual swarm definitions, physical agent concurrency is bounded by the local machine's core capacity and configured concurrency flags. Tasks are scheduled through an in-memory queue that processes subtasks sequentially or in small parallel batches, ensuring rock-solid stability and deterministic progress.

The fourth critical risk is Edge Deployment Incompatibilities and Web Showcase Fragility. Web applications that depend on heavy full-stack frameworks, complex server-side rendering, or bulky node runtimes frequently encounter build failures and slow deployment pipelines on platforms like Vercel or Railway. To mitigate this risk, the Murmur Web Foundry strictly employs a zero-dependency architecture. By utilizing standard semantic HTML5, pure CSS custom property design systems, and modular native JavaScript, the website requires zero compilation steps. It deploys instantaneously as a static edge application, guaranteeing sub-second initial page loads, maximum Lighthouse scores, and zero server maintenance overhead.

## 3. Verification & Acceptance Criteria

To uphold the integrity of the single-phase discovery tier, Phase One must satisfy five strict, non-negotiable verification gates before any subsequent engineering phase can be planned or scheduled.

The first acceptance gate requires the successful delivery and verification of the Pluggable Provider Subsystem. The codebase must contain `src/providers/types.ts` and `src/providers/client.ts`, providing a fully typed interface for interacting with upstream inference endpoints. The client must successfully resolve API credentials for OpenRouter and MeshAPI exclusively through process environment variables, local untracked environment files, and the macOS Keychain, with zero instances of hardcoded tokens or plaintext token persistence. The automatic routing logic must accurately classify requests into cost-effective scanning models versus high-capability reasoning models, verified via dedicated mock tests in `tests/providers.test.ts`.

The second acceptance gate requires the full operational status of the Three-Tier Experience Cascading Engine. The module `src/harness2/experience.ts` must successfully discover and parse experience records from `murmur/EXPERIENCE.md` within the project root, `.murmur/experience.md` in the user's home directory, and designated ecosystem packs. Unit tests in `tests/experience.test.ts` must verify that repository-specific lessons consistently override global user preferences, that missing files at any tier fail safely without exceptions, and that the resolved memory context is seamlessly injected into the Google Harness squared Propose-Probe-Compose cycle.

The third acceptance gate requires the end-to-end functionality of Semantic Codebase Initialization. The command `murmr init --semantic` must successfully accept optional `--provider` and `--model` parameters, analyze an unfamiliar repository's structure and configuration manifests, invoke the provider synthesis layer, and produce a fully compliant `murmur/` directory structure. Running `murmr doctor` against the generated workspace must return a zero exit code with no schema errors, ensuring that generated skills and instructions conform strictly to Murmur intermediate representation specifications.

The fourth acceptance gate requires Complete Test Suite Preservation and Type Safety. The existing baseline of one hundred and forty-three tests across all existing suites must continue to pass without a single regression or skip. All newly authored test suites—covering providers, experience cascading, and semantic initialization—must pass with one hundred percent reliability. The entire test suite must execute cleanly under Bun in less than two point five seconds, and `bun run typecheck` must complete with zero TypeScript compiler errors.

The fifth acceptance gate requires the Deployment Readiness of the Public Web Foundry. The `website/` directory must contain a complete, standalone web application comprising `index.html`, `style.css`, `app.js`, `vercel.json`, and `package.json`. The web interface must render the Starling Murmuration visual identity flawlessly, execute without JavaScript console warnings or errors, provide an interactive Intermediate Representation compiler demonstration supporting all six target runtimes, and be completely self-contained with zero external runtime or build dependencies, ready for instantaneous edge deployment on Vercel or Railway.
